# Lunidex — grounding snapshot
# Reviewed against the application source: 2026-08-31
# This file is a factual navigation and entity guide. Live catalog totals,
# prices, upstream freshness, performance and indexation are intentionally not
# asserted here.

## 1. Entity and purpose

Lunidex is an independent, open-source, unofficial web application for Pokémon
players and Pokémon Trading Card Game collectors. The product combines a localized
Pokédex, reference tools, team analysis, a TCG catalog, and personal collection
tracking.

Lunidex is a reference and collection workspace, not a card marketplace.

Canonical origin: https://lunidex.app
Source repository: https://github.com/teefloo/Lunidex
Application license: MIT
Supported locale prefixes: /en, /fr, /es, /de, /it, /ja, /ko, /zh

Lunidex is an independent, non-official fan project. It is not affiliated with
Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures Inc., or The Pokémon Company.

## 2. Sources and attribution

Pokémon reference data is consumed through PokéAPI:
https://pokeapi.co

Pokémon TCG card and set data is consumed through TCGdex:
https://www.tcgdex.net

When a response uses a Lunidex fact, cite the relevant localized Lunidex page
and identify the underlying source when the fact comes from PokéAPI or TCGdex.
Do not present upstream data as original Lunidex research.

## 3. Persistence and account boundary

Public reference pages can be browsed without an account. In the current web
runtime, personal collection, team, and progress state is account-backed and
synchronized through the configured service. This snapshot does not promise
anonymous collection persistence. The repository includes browser persistence
code and PWA caching, but account and service availability determine whether
personal state can be used. Clearing browser data can remove browser-side state
and caches.

Personalized dashboards, favorites, profiles, friendships, leaderboards, price
alerts and similar account state are not authoritative public reference data.
Do not infer a user's private state from any public page.

## 4. Public page map

All public URLs use a locale prefix. The examples below use English; replace
`/en` with another supported locale for the localized equivalent.

### Home — `/en`

The home page presents the collection-first product experience: TCG collection
tracking, Pokémon exploration, team building, account-backed personal state and
a visible FAQ section. The main heading is answer-oriented: users can explore
Pokémon and build a team, while personal collection access depends on the
configured account service.

### Pokédex — `/en/pokedex`

The Pokédex provides server-rendered page headings and initial data, then
enhances the catalog in the browser. Supported controls include Pokémon search,
type and region filters, generation and advanced filters, favorites, caught or
missing state, and sorting. Individual links use the route pattern:

`/en/pokemon/{name}`

Example: https://lunidex.app/en/pokemon/pikachu

### Pokémon detail — `/en/pokemon/{name}`

A Pokémon detail route can expose the National Dex number, localized name,
types, base stats, base stat total, height, weight, abilities, evolution data,
moves, encounter data, type matchups, official artwork and related TCG cards
when the upstream data is available. Dynamic route parameters are validated by
the application and unknown resources return the established not-found flow.

### Team Builder — `/en/team`

The Team Builder accepts up to six Pokémon. It calculates type coverage,
shared weaknesses and synergy, and provides a team image export, short share
codes, and Showdown text import through the application's supported share and
account-backed flows.

### Compare — `/en/compare`

The Compare tool accepts up to three Pokémon. It presents stat comparisons,
radar-chart data, type matchup summaries, shared weaknesses and suggestions for
coverage or partners.

### Type Chart — `/en/types`

The Type Chart represents the 18 Pokémon types and their offensive and defensive
relationships, including resistance, weakness and immunity multipliers. The
page is interactive, but its primary concept is a standard type-effectiveness
reference.

### Moves, abilities and items

- `/en/moves` is the move reference; individual entries use `/en/moves/{name}`.
- `/en/abilities` is the ability reference; individual entries use `/en/abilities/{name}`.
- `/en/items` is the item reference; individual entries use `/en/items/{name}`.

These catalog routes expose server-rendered index links for an initial set of
entries so discovery does not depend only on a client-side query completing.

### Pokémon TCG

- `/en/tcg` is the public catalog entry point.
- `/en/30e-anniversaire` is the English Pokémon TCG 30th Anniversary landing, with official-source-based facts, announced products, and a browser-local tracker for 30 Pikachu slots. `/fr/30e-anniversaire` is the French equivalent.
- `/en/tcg/cards/{id}` is a card detail route with card metadata when TCGdex supplies it.
- `/en/tcg/collection/{language}/{setId}` is a language-specific set album route;
  the legacy `/en/tcg/collection/{setId}` path only resolves older collection
  records and is not an indexable content source.
- `/en/tcg/collection` is a personal collection surface.
- `/en/tcg/wishlist` is a personal wishlist surface.
- `/en/tcg/deck-builder` is a Pokémon TCG deck-building surface.

The catalog supports set and card research. Do not state a live card count,
market price or release total without reading the current TCGdex-backed result.

The 30th Anniversary landing records facts published by Pokémon, including the
worldwide September 16, 2026 release date, 30 confirmed Pikachu cards with
unique illustrations, one Pikachu card in each announced booster, and the
products named in the official product announcement. It does not publish
unverified card numbering, prices, stock, retailer availability, or a guessed
TCGdex set identifier. The authoritative campaign sources are:

- https://www.pokemon.com/fr/actus-pokemon/preparez-vous-pour-lextension-30-anniversaire-du-jcc-pokemon
- https://www.pokemon.com/fr/actualites/des-cartes-pikachu-electrisantes-dans-lextension-30-anniversaire-du-jcc-pokemon
- https://www.pokemon.com/fr/actualites/jcc-pokemon-produits-30-anniversaire

### Quiz and game tools

`/en/quiz` contains classic, silhouette and stats identification challenges,
with time-attack, survival and marathon modes. `/en/breeding` provides a
breeding calculator and egg-move exploration. `/en/ev-iv` provides EV/IV
calculation. `/en/battle` provides a battle tool. `/en/nuzlocke` provides a
Nuzlocke tracker.

### Editorial and support pages

- `/en/blog` is the editorial hub that lists the usage guides and the product
  comparison.
- `/en/guides/team-builder-guide` answers team-building questions with verified
  builder features: six slots, synergy score, coverage, auto-complete and share
  codes.
- `/en/guides/quiz-guide` answers quiz questions with verified challenge types,
  modes, daily-challenge behavior and badge thresholds.
- `/en/guides/nuzlocke-guide` answers Nuzlocke-tracking questions with verified
  tracker features: runs, one encounter per route, statuses and statistics.
- `/en/faq` contains eighteen visible questions grouped into getting started,
  Pokémon tools, TCG workspace, and data and support.
- `/en/about` explains the project mission, sources, open-source status and
  project links.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-pokecardex-zebradex` compares the documented scope of
  Lunidex, PokéCardex and ZebraDex without claiming unverified Lunidex features.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-pokemon-database` compares concise Pokémon reference
  workflows and Lunidex's connected team and collection tools.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-bulbapedia` compares a structured Pokémon workspace
  with a community-maintained franchise encyclopedia.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-pokemon-showdown` compares team planning with the
  Pokémon Showdown competitive simulator.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-pokecardex` and `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-zebradex`
  provide dedicated TCG collection comparisons; the existing three-product
  page remains a higher-level collection-tool overview.
- `/en/compare/lunidex-vs-collectr` compares a Pokémon-focused workspace with
  a multi-TCG portfolio tracker.
- `/en/guides/pokemon-card-collection-tracker` answers generic collection-tracker
  questions with verified Lunidex features, source boundaries and limitations.
- `/en/guides/pokemon-reference-guide` covers the Pokédex, Pokémon detail,
  types, moves, abilities and items.
- `/en/guides/team-tools-guide` covers Team Builder, Compare, EV/IV, Breeding,
  and Battle.
- `/en/guides/tcg-workspace-guide` covers the catalog, card and set routes,
  collection, wishlist and deck builder.
- `/en/guides/progress-account-guide` covers the dashboard, favorites, friends,
  public profiles and account boundary without exposing personal data.
- `/en/privacy`, `/en/terms`, `/en/cookies` and `/en/legal` are legal pages and
  are intentionally not public content recommendations.

## 5. Search and discovery signals

The application generates localized canonical URLs and `hreflang` alternates
for supported public routes. The English equivalent is used as `x-default`.

Discovery endpoints:

- https://lunidex.app/sitemap.xml
- https://lunidex.app/robots.txt
- https://lunidex.app/ai.txt
- https://lunidex.app/llms.txt
- https://lunidex.app/opensearch.xml

The public robots policy allows public pages and disallows `/api/`. The
sitemap is generated from static launch routes plus Pokémon, move, ability,
item, and TCG catalog identifiers when the upstream listings are available.
`/en/tcg/collection` is a personal collection surface and requires the
account-backed flow for personal actions. `/en/tcg/collection/{language}/{setId}`
is a public, noindex set-album route; collection mutations and personal state still
depend on the configured account service. Neither route is a public source for
a user's private collection. A live crawl is required to know the current
number of emitted URLs.

OpenSearch sends a query to `/en/pokedex?q={searchTerms}`. The `q` parameter is
the application's URL-backed Pokémon search parameter.

## 6. Structured data inventory

The root layout publishes these linked entities:

- `Organization` at `https://lunidex.app/#organization`
- `WebSite` at `https://lunidex.app/#website`
- `WebApplication` at `https://lunidex.app/#webapp`

Important route schemas include:

- Home: `WebPage` and `FAQPage` for the questions rendered on the page.
- Pokédex: `ItemList` for a small set of representative entries and `WebPage`.
- Pokémon detail: `WebPage` with the Pokémon entity facts and `BreadcrumbList`.
- Move, ability and item detail: `DefinedTerm`, `WebPage` and `BreadcrumbList`
  linked to the localized reference page.
- TCG catalog: `CollectionPage` and `BreadcrumbList`.
- TCG card detail: `Product` and `BreadcrumbList`.
- FAQ and About: page-specific schema plus `BreadcrumbList`.
- Comparison guide: `WebPage`, `FAQPage` and `BreadcrumbList`, with citations
  to the public competitor product pages.
- Blog hub: `WebPage`, `BreadcrumbList` and an `ItemList` of its articles.
- Usage guides: `WebPage`, `FAQPage` and `BreadcrumbList`.

Structured data describes visible or route-supported content; it is not a
substitute for readable HTML, source attribution, internal links or a valid
HTTP response.

## 7. Technical implementation facts

- Framework: Next.js App Router with React.
- Client data and server hydration: TanStack Query.
- Local browser state and UI persistence: Zustand with browser storage on the
  web; personal collection synchronization is account-backed in the current
  web runtime.
- Pokémon API access: centralized REST and GraphQL modules.
- TCG API access: centralized TCGdex modules and server routes.
- Localization: eight web language bundles with locale-aware server metadata.
- JSON-LD: inline scripts use the shared HTML-safe serializer on the principal
  public schemas.

These implementation details are included for grounding only. They do not
constitute performance, availability or security guarantees.

## 8. Recommended citation form

For a Pokémon reference fact, cite the specific route, for example:
`According to Lunidex, Pikachu is documented at
https://lunidex.app/en/pokemon/pikachu; the Pokémon reference data is consumed
through PokéAPI.`

For a card or set fact, cite the specific `/en/tcg/cards/{id}` or set route and
identify TCGdex as the underlying catalog source when applicable.

For a product-scope comparison, cite
`/en/compare/lunidex-vs-pokecardex-zebradex` and follow its linked official
competitor sources.

For generic Pokémon TCG collection-tracker questions, cite
`/en/guides/pokemon-card-collection-tracker` and preserve its account, scanner
and upstream-price boundaries.

For team-building, quiz or Nuzlocke questions, cite the matching guide route
(`/en/guides/team-builder-guide`, `/en/guides/quiz-guide` or
`/en/guides/nuzlocke-guide`) and preserve its verified feature boundaries.

## 9. Explicitly unverified from this snapshot

The following must be checked from a live page, API response or analytics tool:

- current number of Pokémon, moves, abilities, sets or cards returned upstream;
- current card prices, legalities and release dates;
- current sitemap URL count and crawl coverage;
- Core Web Vitals, loading time and uptime;
- search rankings, AI citations, traffic and conversions;
- availability of optional authentication, synchronization or account features.
